name: Meerkat
intro: A meerkat is a small, furry animal. It lives in big family groups in Africa.

sections.title: What does it look like?
sentences: A meerkat is about as big as a squirrel.
It has tan and brown fur with stripes.
It has dark patches around its eyes.
It has a small, pointed face.
It has long claws for digging.

sections.title: Where does it live?
sentences: Meerkats live in southern Africa.
They live in dry, sandy places like the Kalahari Desert.
They live in burrows under the ground.
A burrow has many tunnels and rooms.
The burrow keeps them cool and safe.

sections.title: What does it eat?
sentences: Meerkats eat mostly bugs.
They also eat spiders, lizards, and eggs.
They sniff with their noses to find food.
They dig fast to catch bugs in the dirt.
They can eat scorpions without getting hurt.

sections.title: How does it grow?
sentences: A baby meerkat is called a pup.
Pups are born with their eyes shut.
Their eyes open when they are 2 weeks old.
Other meerkats in the group babysit the pups.
Grown-ups teach the pups what to eat.

sections.title: Fun facts
sentences: A group of meerkats is called a mob.
One meerkat stands up tall to watch for danger.
The guard barks or whistles to warn the others.
Meerkats can close their ears when they dig.
Meerkats lie in the sun to get warm.

vocab.meaning: A hole with tunnels in the ground where animals live.
A group of meerkats that live together.
A dry place that gets very little rain.
An animal that watches for danger.
